rounds.text: Meesho is demonstrating aggressive market capture, evidenced by compounded sales growth of 40% over the trailing twelve months [E14], significantly outpacing the sector median sales growth of 14.4% [E60]. This top-line momentum is supported by a clear improvement in operational efficiency, with quarterly operating margins expanding by 9 percentage points year-over-year as of September 2026 [E20]. Institutional confidence is surging, as evidenced by a combined 13.85 percentage point increase in holdings by foreign and domestic institutions since December 2025 [E31, E32], resulting in a positive money flow signal [E33]. The company maintains a fortress balance sheet with a debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.01x [E26] and total borrowings reduced to Rs 49 Cr [E28]. Conceded: the company faces significant valuation and profitability headwinds, including a P/B ratio of 27.94x [E1], negative ROE of -46.2% [E12], and negative free cash flow of Rs -3,976 Cr [E25]. Despite these challenges, the stock’s technical strength is undeniable, currently trading at a relative-strength rating of 100 against the Nifty 500 [E37] and holding above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E36].

The valuation of Meesho Ltd is disconnected from its fundamental performance, as evidenced by a price-to-book ratio of 27.94x, which significantly exceeds the sector benchmark of 2.14x [E1, E6]. This extreme premium is difficult to justify given that the company is currently destroying shareholder capital, evidenced by a return on equity of -46.2% and a return on capital employed of -40.0% [E11, E12]. Furthermore, the company is burning cash at an alarming rate, with free cash flow reaching -Rs 3,976 Cr in March 2026 [E25]. While sales growth is present, the company’s inability to translate this into profit is highlighted by a -20% compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months [E14, E16]. Conceded: the company maintains a strong balance sheet with minimal debt and has seen positive institutional money flow [E26, E33]. Despite these technical tailwinds, the stock’s 55.0% annualized volatility and the fact that it is trading near its 52-week high suggest that the market has already priced in aggressive expectations that the current negative operating margins and inconsistent profit trends may struggle to meet [E19, E21, E35, E39].

The bear’s focus on the price-to-book ratio [E1, E6] ignores the rapid transformation in operational efficiency, as evidenced by the quarterly operating margin improving by 9 percentage points in September 2026 compared to the year-ago quarter [E20]. While the bear highlights negative returns [E11, E12], it fails to acknowledge that the company is successfully scaling, with compounded sales growth accelerating to 40% over the trailing twelve months [E14]. Conceded: the company reported negative free cash flow of Rs -3,976 Cr [E25] and a -20% compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months [E16]. However, this capital expenditure is clearly being rewarded by the market, as evidenced by the stock trading at 96% of its 52-week range and maintaining a perfect relative-strength rating of 100 against the Nifty 500 [E34, E37]. Furthermore, the bear’s concern regarding volatility [E39] is countered by the fact that the stock maintains a healthy Sharpe ratio of 1.08, indicating that the risk is being compensated by performance [E40]. Finally, the massive influx of institutional capital, with foreign and domestic holdings increasing by 5.53 and 8.32 percentage points respectively, demonstrates that sophisticated investors are prioritizing the company's aggressive growth trajectory over current accounting losses [E31, E32, E33].

The bull’s reliance on a single quarter of margin improvement [E20] ignores the broader reality of an inconsistent operating-margin trend [E21, E22] and a long-term decline in operating margins from -6% to -8% over three years [E19]. While the bull points to sales growth [E14], it fails to address that this expansion is currently value-destructive, as evidenced by a severe -46.2% return on equity [E12] and a median three-year ROE of -63% [E17]. Conceded: the stock shows strong relative strength [E37] and institutional buying [E33]. However, this price performance is decoupled from fundamental health, as the company continues to burn cash with a negative free cash flow of Rs -3,976 Cr [E25] and a negative operating cash flow [E24]. The bull’s claim that risk is compensated by performance [E40] is undermined by the company's extreme annualised volatility of 55.0% [E39] and a valuation that sits at a staggering 27.94x book value [E1, E45]. Ultimately, the market's current enthusiasm ignores the fact that the company is failing to generate profit, with compounded profit growth at -20% [E16] and a return on capital employed of -40.0% [E11].
